# Generated Artifact with a Pristine Source

The file the application loads is **generated**, carries a DO-NOT-EDIT banner naming its generator,
and its **input is committed beside it**. Three things must all be true, and it is the third that
distinguishes this from ordinary code generation: in a normal build the source is the only thing in
the repo and the artifact is gitignored. Here **both are tracked**, because the artifact must load
from `file://` with no build step available — see [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]].

Confirmed in three repositories.

## The three instances

| Repo | Generated | Pristine source | Generator |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IT Applications in Business and Commerce` | `lecture/exam_prep/chapters.js` (567 lines, 497 questions) | `chapters.backup.js` (454 lines) | `_build_bank.js` |
| `Physics` | `exam_prep/js/quizsets.js` | `exam_prep/js/data.js` | `tools/build_sets.mjs` |
| `Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories` | `lab6_Neo4j/viewer/js/data.js` | `lab6_Neo4j/global_finance.csv` | *not committed* |

The banner is the tell, and it says the same thing in two repos five weeks apart:

> "// GENERATED by _build_bank.js — DO NOT hand-edit. Edit chapters.backup.js (study) or the"
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/lecture/exam_prep/chapters.js, 2026-07-10

> "/* AUTO-GENERATED by tools/build_sets.mjs — do not hand-edit."
> — Physics/exam_prep/js/quizsets.js, 2026-07-10

Both banners go further than forbidding edits: they name the file to edit *instead*, and the exact
command to regenerate. A banner without those two facts sends the reader hunting.

## What the generators actually do

Not templating. In each case the generator performs a transformation that would be error-prone or
tedious by hand, and each one is deterministic so re-runs are stable:

- **`_build_bank.js`** merges a synthetic study bank with a dirty past-exam dump, **de-duplicates**
  (~169 raw items where concepts repeated up to six times, collapsed to one well-formed question
  each), **de-biases option order** so the answer is not guessable by position, reassigns global ids,
  and applies four documented answer-key corrections. Determinism comes from an LCG seeded `1337`.
- **`build_sets.mjs`** partitions a question bank by **Jaccard similarity** to a provided set — set 2
  is the 16 most similar, set 3 the 59 least similar, i.e. the coverage gaps — and writes an audit
  report alongside.
- The Discrete-Maths viewer converts a CSV into the `PAWLAK` object of a
  [[pawlak-information-system]], so an offline viewer can reproduce the Neo4j lab without a database.

The one asymmetry: only the first two commit their generator. The Neo4j viewer's `data.js` states its
input (`global_finance.csv`, which *is* in the tree) but the converting script is absent, so that
instance is regenerable in principle and not in practice.

## Why the source is "pristine" and not just "the input"

`_build_bank.js` reloads the backup rather than the generated file on every run — deliberately, and
it says so:

> "// ---- load synthetic bank (ALWAYS from the pristine backup, never the generated file) ----"
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/lecture/exam_prep/_build_bank.js, 2026-07-10

That single line is what prevents the classic failure: regenerate from the output once and the
de-biasing, de-duplication and id reassignment compound on already-processed data. The word
"backup" in the filename is misleading — `chapters.backup.js` is not a backup, it is the source of
truth, and the file that *looks* authoritative is the derived one.

## Where it sits

Three of the instances are exam-prep apps, so this is a component of
[[course-as-runnable-study-tool]]. The broader form — one dataset, many outputs, generator owns all
of them — is [[single-source-of-truth-generators]]. Keeping both files in the tree is also a mild
case of [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]], though here the retained copy is load-bearing rather
than vestigial.
